transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you too, Dr. Smith. Well, I came in today because... I've started to feel, in this quiet but really stubborn way, that the best version of my life is just behind me now. I'm used to being able to figure things out, but lately it feels like no amount of planning or discipline is going to get me back to feeling like myself. I just can't seem to shake that feeling, so I thought it was time to talk to someone about it.
Have you ever felt this way during any other period in your life before now?

No, not really. I mean, I've had stressful times before, of course—back when I was working, or during my studies years ago. But I always bounced back from those once the situation resolved. 

This current feeling, where it just sort of drags on and I can't seem to shake it... no, I haven't experienced this before. It's new for me.
How long have you been feeling this way?
Well, it's been quite a while. This has been going on since I had a hiking injury... that was a little over three years ago. I'd say it's been about three years and three months now, to be specific.
During these past three years, have there been any periods of two months or longer where you felt completely like your usual self, without these feelings of sadness or low mood?
No, I don't think so. I mean, I might have a good day here and there, but... no, definitely not two whole months. It's just been pretty much a constant thing in the background ever since it started.
Over these past three years, have you noticed a persistent change in your appetite, either eating much more or much less than you used to?
No, I haven't noticed any real change there. I mean, I still eat about the same amount as I always have. My appetite has been pretty steady through all of this, really.
Have you noticed any persistent changes in your sleep patterns, such as difficulty falling asleep, staying asleep, or sleeping significantly more than usual, during these past three years?

No, not really. My sleep has been pretty normal, actually. I mean, I usually just go to bed and sleep through the night fine. I haven't had any trouble falling asleep or felt like I'm sleeping too much, so... no, no real changes there either.
During these past three years, have you frequently felt like you are not good enough or lacked confidence in yourself?

No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I know who I am and what I've accomplished... I retired a few years back after a long career, and I feel fine about all that. It's just this constant low mood, you know? But my confidence... no, that hasn't really taken a hit. I don't feel worthless or anything like that.
During these past three years, have you felt a persistent sense of low energy or fatigue?

Yes, I have. I mean, I still get up every day and do what needs doing... I do the shopping, I tinker with some projects around the house. But it just feels like... well, even the small things take a lot out of me. Like, if I'm setting up for a mentoring session, or just walking through a community event, I end up feeling completely worn out. And it's the kind of tired that a nap doesn't really fix, you know? It just sort of lingers.
During these past three years, have you found it difficult to concentrate on things or make decisions?

No, my concentration is fine. I haven't noticed any trouble focusing on things or making decisions. Like I said, I still do my mentoring and work on my projects, and I can stay on task with all of that just fine. It's really just the low mood and the fatigue. Decisions aren't any harder for me now than they ever were.
During these past three years, have you lost interest or pleasure in the activities that you used to enjoy?

No, I wouldn't say I've lost interest. I still enjoy the things I've always liked doing. I still like mentoring the younger folks, and I still get satisfaction out of my projects around the house. It's just that I feel tired while I'm doing them, and my mood is just... flat. But the actual enjoyment of the activities, that's still there. I haven't lost that.
Do you feel a sense of hopelessness about the future?

Yes, I suppose I do. That's actually why I decided to come in. I've just started to feel—in a very quiet but stubborn sort of way—that the best version of my life is already behind me. It just seems like no amount of planning or discipline is ever going to get me back to feeling like myself again.
